translation.english_text: Sir! My child and I are starving.
Don't you understand when you're told once?

notes: `கோடி புண்ணியம்` is kept as religious merit rather than converted into a material reward.
translation.english_text: Sir, a crore-fold merit to you...

source_locator.description: Kalyani catches hold of Sekar's feet.

notes: `புண்ணியம் பார்த்துப் பார்த்துத்தான்` is rhetorically pressure-sensitive; the first-pass English keeps the repeated merit wording rather than supplying an unstated explanation.
The kick is embedded in the immutable dialogue record and remains inside the same unit.
translation.english_text: It is by looking after merit again and again that I have ended up unable even to see my younger sister's face. (Saying this, he kicks Kalyani away.)

notes: The invective preserves the source's sibling appeal, hunger image, `பரட்டைத் தலை`, cotton-in-the-eyes metaphor, and `பாவம்... புண்ணியம்... நாசம்` sequence without smoothing them into a new argument.
translation.english_text: Ah, sinners! Were you people not born with brothers and sisters? Even after seeing my little child writhing with hunger, even after seeing this dishevelled head—sinners! Have your eyes been stuffed with cotton? O embodiments of non-violence who speak of sin... merit... ruin—if there is such a thing as ruin, that alone will be the fitting place for you. It will be the fitting place for you.

source_locator.description: Kalyani is driven away by the servant.

translation.english_text: (Kalyani is driven away by the servant.)

notes: The source's `உன் அப்பாவும் மாமாவும் இருந்தால் நீதான் உன் அப்பாவை கர்ப்பத்திலே விழுங்கி விட்டாயே` is left structurally close and deliberately not rationalized into a biographical explanation.
The source says that both mother and child were beaten; the English retains that wording even though the immediately preceding visible action explicitly kicks Kalyani.
translation.english_text: Dear child! This world submits to pomp and wickedness! There is no place for us to live in this world. What are you looking at? Are you looking to see whether the tears running from my eyes might be milk? Your father should have seen you and me being beaten; your maternal uncles should have seen it. If your father and uncles were here... you yourself swallowed your father in the womb! My beauty? Are you hungry? Don't cry. I myself cannot bear the hunger; how can I bear your voice? Come, let's go.
